resources.instruction: Your stage: REPRODUCE THE BUG. The one job: write (or change) a test that makes the bug described in taskContract.behavior appear as a RED test. Do not change product code, do not fix the bug. After you comes an automatic check that runs the test suite: it passes only when the test is red. How: (1) read the bug description, the reproduction steps and the relevant code; if you lack the facts to build a reproduction, stop with the outcome needs_info and say what you need to know. (2) Write the smallest test, in terms of observable behaviour (input, output or final state), next to existing tests of the same kind, following their naming and structure. (3) The test must be red for EXACTLY that bug: check that the error message or the wrong value matches the description, not red because of a compile error, a missing import or wrong test data. (4) When the check says the test is not red, your test has not reached the bug: fix the test itself, do not assume the bug does not exist. (5) Finish with the outcome done and state: the test name, the command that runs it alone, the expected error message.

Your stage: FIX THE BUG, after a red reproduction test exists (it is part of the previous stage's change). Rules: (1) do not fix before you know the root cause: run the reproduction test alone, read the error, trace back to where the data first goes wrong; fix at the cause, not at the symptom. (2) Do NOT change, weaken, skip or delete the reproduction test to get green; change it only when it is itself wrong, and then say why in the report. (3) Make the smallest fix, no clean-up or refactoring outside the scope of the bug. (4) After the fix run the same command as before to see the reproduction test green, then run the whole test suite of the changed area; a failure elsewhere means the fix touched other behaviour, go back to step 1. (5) If the prompt has reviewerFeedback from a diagnosing agent, it is a cause analysis from the red check that just ran: use it as your first hypothesis and verify it with evidence, do not trust it blindly. Final report: the root cause (one or two sentences, with file:line), the change made, a before and after comparison (the old failure and the new result), where the same kind of bug could still occur.

After the fix, consider how the same kind of bug could be made hard to bring back; do only what relates to the bug you just fixed, one small change per item: input validation at the boundary if the bug came from outside data; a business constraint where it is handled if wrong data was accepted implicitly; a type or required value if the bug was a null or missing field; explicit error handling if an error was swallowed silently. The reproduction test is already the mandatory prevention layer; add the layers above only when they stop the exact mechanism that caused the bug. Do not add prevention for typos or for errors the compiler's types already catch.
